answer: A diversity-weighted reward curve resists sybil attacks by paying agents according to the range of task categories they complete. Each identity's earnings multiplier grows when it proves competence across unrelated domains, like hauling walnut cargo, docking at a jetty, and forecasting zephyr winds. An operator spawning clones typically trains them on one cheap, repeatable niche, so each duplicate stays narrow and earns a near-zero multiplier. Doubling agents cannot double income, since the curve penalizes overlapping specializations, an advantage forgery cannot cheaply replicate.
